text:
anya: Quick heads-up — ran a mixed-seqlen benchmark this morning and the numbers look suspicious. bimodal workloads (short ~64 tokens + long ~1024 tokens) are showing strange prefill->decode spillover at p99.

matt: Can you paste the profile?

anya: Pasted below from perf collector. model=xgen-7b, kernels autotuned.

perf-bot: ```
run: 2025-11-02T07:12Z
batch_size_distribution: { 4: 60%, 8: 30%, 16: 10% }
seqlen_distribution: { short: 64 (70%), long: 1024 (30%) }
aggregate: p50=45ms p95=210ms p99=620ms
breakdown (avg): prefill=22ms decode=23ms
p99 breakdown sample: prefill=30ms decode=480ms
kv_cache_hit_rate: 78% overall, 42% for long tails
kernel_choices: prefill=gpu-opt-v2 decode=gpu-opt-v1 (fallback on kv-miss)
```

jordan: Whoa decode p99 ballooning to 480ms while avg decode ~23ms. Sounds like microbatching + KV miss interactions.

anya: My hypothesis: scheduler coalesces short and long requests into same microbatch, kernel selected for short-prefill fast-path, decode side gets long sequences but without decode-optimized kernel -> slower and kv-cache misses exacerbate.

sophia: Do we have traces that show microbatch composition over time?

anya: Yes, here's a quick sample from the trace log (trimmed):
```
[09:12:03.122] mbatch_id=abc seqs=[64,64,64,1024] schedule->prefill kernel=gpu-opt-v2
[09:12:03.156] prefill done, decode started kernel=gpu-opt-v2
[09:12:03.158] kv-miss for request#4, fetching... +120ms
[09:12:03.280] decode long tail running on gpu-opt-v2 (not ideal) +300ms
```

kumar: So kernel selection stuck to prefill's pick. We should consider dynamic kernel switch at stage boundary if batch contains long sequences. Currently runtime enforces single kernel choice per microbatch to avoid memory thrashing.

matt: We already have an early prototype for split-kernel microbatches but turned it off because of async copy overhead. Could be worth revisiting if p99 is that bad.

jordan: Alternative: tweak batching heuristics so we don't mix long sequences with shorts. E.g., prefer homogeneous microbatches for seqlen or cap microbatch size when long seq present.

anya: I ran a quick experiment: prefer-homogeneous flag on scheduler -> p99 dropped from 620ms to ~320ms, overall p95 little changed. Works but throughput down ~8%.

perf-bot: Small run summary with prefer-homogeneous=true:
```
throughput: -8%
p50=48ms p95=200ms p99=320ms
kv_hit_rate unchanged
```

sophia: That's promising. Tradeoff looks reasonable for latency-sensitive tiers. Maybe expose as policy per route.

matt: Another angle: kernel autotuner could pick decode-optimized kernel when any seq>512 present. That reduces decode time for long tails but we need to guard prefill regressions for short-only batches.

anya: Right — test showed switching kernel to decode-opt when long present reduced the long decode p99 to ~230ms, but prefill for short-only batches in that microbatch went up ~6ms. Net: p50 unaffected, p99 improved.

kumar: We should probably implement a fallback rule: if mixing unavoidable, split long seqs into separate microbatches asynchronously and prioritize KV warmup pre-decode. Warmup could prefetch top-k KV entries for predicted tokens.

jordan: Prefetching KV for long tails sounds heavy. But maybe a lightweight heuristic: if seqlen>512 schedule a warmup job that touches KV pages before decode. That could hide HBM page faults.

matt: Also verify quantized kernel codepaths — some of them allocate larger temp buffers and cause transient GC-like stalls for mixed batches. I saw a regression last month where quantized decode did an occasional 200ms stall with sparse KV misses.

anya: Agreed. Action items I propose:
- short-term: enable scheduler policy 'prefer-homogeneous' for latency-critical routes (canary config)
- mid-term: prototype split-kernel microbatching at stage boundary (only for microbatches with long tails)
- investigation: instrument KV fetch latencies per-request and track correlation with kernel choice and temp buffer allocations

sophia: I'll add a console dashboard panel for microbatch composition + per-kernel p99 next sprint.

kumar: I'll put together a microbenchmark that simulates bimodal seq distributions and exercises kernel-switch and prefetch strategies.

matt: I'll dig into the autotuner code to allow sequence-aware kernel decisions (rule-based override).

anya: Cool. One more datapoint from the run: when we raised microbatch cap from 16->24 throughput rose ~5% but p99 increased 40%. So microbatch size tuning has nonlinear tail effects. Documenting that in the playbook would help SREs pick sensible defaults.

jordan: Can we add an alert: if p99_decode >> p95_decode by factor >5 and kv_miss_rate > 30% then create perf incident? That would catch regressions early.

anya: Yep. I'll draft a short RFC with experiment results and recommended defaults. Posting notes in #eng-runtime after I collate logs. Thanks all :thumbsup:

matt: :+1:

perf-bot: nightly profiler scheduled. next run in 12h.
